Trading isn’t complicated—clarity is what’s rare. Here’s how to get it right:

1. Stop chasing instant wealth.  
2. Embrace randomness—it’s part of the game.  
3. Pick one setup.  
4. Delete the other five.  
5. Risk less than you’re comfortable with.  
6. Halve your position size.  
7. Then halve it again.  
8. Stop watching PnL while the trade is live.  
9. Set your risk before entering.  
10. Never push a stop further away.  
11. Know your win rate.  
12. Know your average risk-reward.  
13. Know your worst historical drawdown.  
14. Be ready, emotionally, for twice that.  
15. Step away when tired.  
16. Step away when emotional.  
17. Step away after revenge impulses.  
18. Don’t trade to feel productive.  
19. Don’t trade to kill boredom.  
20. Learn to do nothing.  
21. Learn to miss moves—without reacting.  
22. Accept you’ll never catch every opportunity.  
23. Accept FOMO is self-sabotage.  
24. Don’t increase size after wins.  
25. Don’t increase size after losses.  
26. Journal your emotional state, not just trades.  
27. Spot your tilt pattern.  
28. Identify what triggers self-sabotage.  
29. Remove that trigger.  
30. Build a consistent daily routine.  
31. Sleep well.  
32. Train your body.  
33. Manage caffeine.  
34. Breathe before pulling the trigger.  
35. Separate self-worth from PnL.  
36. Let go of needing to be right.  
37. Accept losses calmly.  
38. Let winners run—according to plan.  
39. Stop micromanaging open trades.  
40. Backtest with at least 200 samples.  
41. Forward test with tiny size.  
42. Prove consistency before scaling.  
43. Grow position size slowly.  
44. Never scale based on emotion.  
45. Track in R-multiples, not dollars.  
46. Focus on process, not results.  
47. Measure execution quality.  
48. Grade yourself weekly.  
49. Fix one mistake at a time.  
50. Stay with your strategy—no hopping.  
51. Avoid indicator overload.  
52. Avoid over-optimizing.  
53. Don’t copy random traders.  
54. Build conviction through data.  
55. Trade one session.  
56. Trade one instrument.  
57. Master one timeframe.  
58. Understand volatility context.  
59. Define when not to trade.  
60. Define clear invalidation rules.  
61. Accept missed profits.  
62. Respect your max daily loss limit.  
63. Stop trading when you hit it.  
64. Step away after emotional spikes.  
65. Review screenshots daily.  
66. Study losers more than winners.  
67. Check if you’re cutting winners too early.  
68. Check if you’re holding losers too long.  
69. Fix that imbalance.  
70. Protect capital aggressively.  
71. Treat capital like inventory.  
72. Understand position sizing math.  
73. Respect compounding.  
74. Avoid all-in bets.  
75. Avoid “this is the one” thinking.  
76. Trade like a statistician.  
77. Build tolerance for drawdowns.  
78. Accept flat months.  
79. Accept slow growth.  
80. Accept boredom.  
81. Build patience deliberately.  
82. Train focus daily.  
83. Reduce dopamine dependence.  
84. Avoid constant comparison.  
85. Stop hunting for holy grails.  
86. Accept—you’re the main variable.  
87. Accept—psychology outweighs entries.  
88. Accept uncertainty—forever.  
89. Protect the downside first.  
90. Scale only after proven consistency.  
91. Never trade to recover losses.  
92. Never trade to prove a point.  
93. Never trade to escape reality.  
94. Trade only to execute your plan.  
95. Stay small until you’re stable.  
96. Prioritize survival over speed.  
97. Build emotional stability before size.  
98. Respect your system—even when bored.  
99. Think in years, not days.  
100. Stay in the game long enough for probability to work.

Thailand. From September 15, visa-free stay is 30 days again, not 60

The special 60-day regime that was granted to citizens of about 93 countries since July 2024 is being cancelled. The new rules will start from September 15, 2026. Until this date, 60 days are still given at the border.

What's changing:
• Most countries, including Russia, USA, EU, UK, Australia - visa-free stay of 30 days.
• Seychelles and Mauritius - 15 days.
• Visa on Arrival is being limited; countries like Azerbaijan, Belarus, Serbia remain on the list.
• Those already in the country on a 60-day stamp can complete their stay. There is no retroactive effect.
• DTV, LTR, Privilege, work, pension - remain unchanged.

Why: in May, the government decided to close the gap for visa-runners, nominal tourists, and those living in the country for months. The usual package vacation (~9 days) is almost unaffected.
For Russians, the visa-free stay is not being canceled - they are simply returning to the old 30-day limit under a bilateral agreement.

In August, institutional investors poured record yearly inflows into crypto funds: +$3.3B in BTC and +$1.5B in ETH. Interest in BTC and ETH remains high.

When rates rise, money can flow into more conservative assets like gold or bonds. Crypto and equities may come under pressure as a result.

📌 UTXO Model: Why Bitcoin Doesn’t Count Coins Like a Simple Balance

Main Points
⏺ In the UTXO model, a wallet holds many separate “coin pieces,” not one shared balance
⏺ Every spend consumes old outputs and creates new ones
⏺ This post explains why one transfer can be built from multiple parts

1️⃣ Core Idea — coins exist as unspent outputs from previous transactions.
2️⃣ How Spending Works — your wallet selects outputs, sends part to the recipient, and returns change back to you.
3️⃣ Why It Matters — fees depend on transaction size, not just amount; many small inputs can cost more.
4️⃣ Privacy Angle — combining several outputs in one transaction can link addresses together.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — avoid collecting too much dust and remember that a big balance may be made of many small pieces.

Final Thoughts

In Bitcoin, balance isn’t one number in a box — it’s a set of coin fragments. When you pay, your wallet assembles them and sends change back.

A data leak has linked the real identities of 291 crypto users directly to their wallet activity, stripping away the anonymity they relied on.

Copied support records exposed varying combinations of personal identity, location, and compliance data. Private keys and customer funds were not compromised in the incident.

The breach highlights a persistent vulnerability in crypto: while blockchain transactions can be pseudonymous, KYC and compliance records held by centralized services create a paper trail that, if exposed, can permanently de-anonymize users.

⚠️ Bitcoin mining divide pushes Luke Dashjr out of OCEAN 

📣 OCEAN co-founder Luke Dashjr left the Bitcoin mining pool on Aug. 29 after reaching a mutual separation agreement with its parent company, Mummolin Inc. He resigned as chairman, chief technology officer and director. OCEAN and Dashjr attributed the separation to “different visions for the future of Bitcoin mining following the recent protocol developments.” The statement did not identify the developments or explain the areas of disagreement.

📊 The wording therefore does not confirm whether a single Bitcoin protocol proposal caused the split. Dashjr has participated in public debates about transaction policies, mining decentralization and alternative Bitcoin software. Connecting the departure to any particular dispute would require further confirmation from the parties. Dashjr had already stepped back from his OCEAN responsibilities earlier in August. His permanent departure now removes him from the company’s leadership and ownership structure.

🌐 The company did not announce a replacement chairman or chief technology officer. It also provided no details about how Dashjr’s former technical responsibilities will be distributed. Dashjr plans to create a new venture called CONVOY. The joint statement said the project would continue his mission of decentralizing Bitcoin mining.

📌 HOW WITHDRAWALS WORK IN METATRONICS

There are two separate steps when withdrawing funds from AI Trading.
This is important to understand:

1. Exit funds from trading
2. Withdraw funds to an external wallet

These are not the same process.

Step 1: Exit from Trading Wallet

When you activate AI Trading, your funds are allocated to the Trading Wallet and participate in trading operations.

To return these funds from trading, open your Trading Wallet and select Request Withdrawal.

You will then choose a trading exit option.

The faster you want to exit trading, the higher the commission:

• Fastest exit: 10%
• 2 days: 5%
• 4 days: 3%
• 6 days: 2%
• 10 days: 0%

Once this process is completed, the funds return from the Trading Wallet to your available balance.

Step 2: Withdraw to your external wallet

After the funds become available for withdrawal, you can submit a separate request to send them to your external crypto wallet.

This withdrawal can take up to 24 hours to process.

The full process looks like this:

Trading Wallet → Trading Exit → Available Balance → Withdrawal Request → External Wallet

⚠️ Important

The fastest trading exit option does not mean that funds are instantly transferred to your external wallet.

It means that you choose the fastest available way to remove funds from the trading process.

The transfer to your external wallet is a separate step and may take up to 24 hours.

METATRONICS does not offer guaranteed instant withdrawals.

Even the fastest available trading exit option requires processing time and is not guaranteed to be immediate.
